editorial.headline: Porcelain Sanitaryware Is Fully Open, Including in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 23934 covers the manufacture of porcelain sanitary fixtures, open across all business scales and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 23934 is a manufacturing category for porcelain sanitary equipment. Its scope is practical and material-specific: the making of sanitary fixtures from porcelain, including toilets, bidets, washbasins, urinals, sinks, and bathtubs. This is not a catch-all for bathroom trading, installation, or services; the record points to industrial production of the porcelain fixtures themselves.

The code is open to every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the activity can be registered by very small operators as well as larger manufacturers, provided the registration matches the actual activity being carried out. For a founder, the key editorial point is to treat the product scope carefully. The code is anchored in porcelain sanitary equipment, so the commercial story should begin with what is made, not merely where the products are sold or used.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clean. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership figure of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, a PMA structure is nationally open for this activity, and the record does not impose a lower foreign-share cap. There is no basis here to invent a special threshold, minimum capital figure, extra licence, tax treatment, or timeline. The national reading is simply that foreign ownership may reach 100% under the cited investment-list source.

The Bali picture is also unusually direct. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis, but this record says KBLI 23934 is not blocked by that moratorium. The reason given is that at Besar scale the OSS risk sits in the Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi band, which keeps it outside the blocked Low and Medium-Low category. So the honest conclusion is not a warning that foreigners are barred in Bali; it is the reverse. Based on this slim record, porcelain sanitaryware manufacturing is nationally open to PMA and not moratorium-blocked in Bali.
